sectionsContent.title: Unit 5 Study Guide: Molecular Structure & Polarity

concept.summary: Work each section, then check it against your notes. Anything you miss tells you what to practise before the test. The back is a practice version of the written test. EN: H 2.20 · C 2.55 · O 3.44 · F 3.98.

blocks.label: S4.5–S4.6 · BOND TYPES
answers: How strongly an atom pulls on shared electrons.

blocks.label: S5.1 · LEWIS STRUCTURES
prompts: How do you find an element's number of valence electrons from the periodic table? How many does chlorine have?
Which atom goes in the center of a Lewis structure? Why is H never the center?
List the four steps for drawing a Lewis structure.
The center atom has fewer than 8 electrons and none are left to place. What do you do?
Name the octet-rule exceptions from class.
answers: For main-group elements, use the last digit of the group number. Chlorine is in group 17, so it has 7.
The atom with the lowest electronegativity (not counting H). H can only make one bond, and the center atom bonds to every other atom.
Count all valence e⁻. Skeleton: center atom, single bonds. Fill: lone pairs on outer atoms (leftovers on the center). Check: center short? Make a double bond.
Turn a lone pair on an outer atom into a second (or third) bond with the center: a double or triple bond.
Boron is stable with 6 and beryllium with 4. Atoms in period 3 and below can hold more than 8 (phosphorus can make 5 bonds and hold 10).

blocks.label: S5.2–S5.3 · VSEPR & SHAPES
prompts: What does VSEPR stand for, and what is its main idea?
Why do lone pairs make bond angles smaller?
A central atom has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair. Name its electron geometry and its molecular shape. Why are they different?
answers: Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion: electron groups around the center push as far apart as they can.
Lone pairs repel more strongly than bonding pairs, so they push the bonds closer together.
Electron geometry: tetrahedral (4 groups). Molecular shape: trigonal pyramidal. The shape is named only by where the atoms are; the lone pair takes up space but is not part of the name.
blocks.heading: Shapes, Polarity & Symmetry

blocks.label: S5.4 · POLARITY
prompts: What is the difference between bond polarity and molecular polarity?
How can a molecule with polar bonds still be nonpolar?
Why do lone pairs on the central atom usually make a molecule polar?
answers: Bond polarity is one bond, set by ΔEN. Molecular polarity is the whole molecule, set by the bond polarity AND the shape.
When the polar bonds are arranged symmetrically (evenly around the center), their pulls cancel.
They make the shape lopsided (asymmetric), so the bond pulls do not cancel.

keyNotes: No compound on this guide appears on any version of the test. Symmetry check: CCl₄, BBr₃, C₂H₂ are even, so the pulls cancel; PCl₃ (lone pair), CHCl₃ (one different atom) and NOCl are lopsided. Back chart: scored like the test, 7 per compound.
